description: Create the two new ML modules — outfit_compatibility_transformer.py and preference_reward_model.py — plus preference_dataset.py, with their unit tests. These are entirely self-contained: they have no dependency on recommendation_agent.py and can be implemented and tested independently of FEAT-002.
steps: 1. Create backend/app/ml/outfit_compatibility_transformer.py. Implement OutfitCompatibilityTransformer(nn.Module): learnable positional embedding nn.Embedding(10, 512); TransformerEncoder with encoder_layer(d_model=512, nhead=4, dim_feedforward=1024, dropout=0.1, batch_first=True), num_layers=2; mean pooling; MLP head Linear(512,256)->ReLU->Dropout(0.1)->Linear(256,1)->Sigmoid. Implement train_on_polyvore_style_data(positive_pairs, negative_pairs) using BCELoss + Adam(lr=1e-4), 10 epochs, batch_size=32 (or all data if smaller), CPU only. Implement score_outfit(embeddings: list[np.ndarray]) -> float: stacks as tensor shape (1, N, 512), adds positional encodings for positions 0..N-1, runs forward, returns Python float. Implement module-level load_or_init() using ARTIFACT_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'artifacts' / 'outfit_transformer.pt'; torch.load with weights_only=True if exists. Implement save_model(model) -> None. Wrap all torch operations in try/except; score_outfit returns 0.5 if torch unavailable.

2. Create backend/tests/test_outfit_compatibility_transformer.py. Tests: (a) score_outfit with N=2,3,5 random np arrays of shape (512,) returns float in [0,1]. (b) load_or_init with monkeypatched ARTIFACT_PATH pointing to a tmp_path that does not contain the file returns an instance without error. (c) train_on_polyvore_style_data with 4 positives and 4 negatives (lists of [np.array(512)] per outfit) completes without error. (d) save_model writes a file, load_or_init reloads it, score_outfit before and after reload produces the same value on the same input. Use np.random.default_rng(0) for all random data. All tests run on CPU.

3. Create backend/app/ml/preference_reward_model.py. Implement PreferenceRewardModel(nn.Module): self._trained = False attribute; MLP Linear(512,256)->ReLU->Dropout(0.1)->Linear(256,128)->ReLU->Linear(128,1) (no final activation). Implement train_from_feedback(feedback_pairs: list[tuple[list[np.ndarray], list[np.ndarray]]]) -> None: mean-pool each outfit's embeddings to a single 512-d tensor; Bradley-Terry loss L = -log(sigmoid(R(preferred) - R(rejected))); Adam lr=1e-4, 20 epochs; sets self._trained = True on success. Implement predict_reward(embeddings: list[np.ndarray]) -> float: mean-pool to 512-d, forward pass, return raw scalar (unbounded). Implement load_or_init(user_id: str) -> PreferenceRewardModel: ARTIFACT_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'artifacts' / f'reward_model_{user_id[:8]}.pt'; torch.load with weights_only=True if exists, sets _trained=True on loaded model. Implement save(self, user_id: str). Wrap all torch in try/except; predict_reward returns 0.0 if unavailable.

4. Create backend/tests/test_preference_reward_model.py. Tests: (a) predict_reward on list of 3 random 512-d arrays returns a Python float. (b) load_or_init with missing artifact path returns a model with _trained=False. (c) train_from_feedback with 2 pairs sets _trained=True and runs without error. (d) Bradley-Terry loss decreases: compute loss at epoch 0 vs epoch 20 using 4 pairs; assert loss_final < loss_initial. (e) save + load_or_init round-trip: predict_reward on same input before and after reload is identical (approx). Use np.random.default_rng(0), tmp_path fixture for save path.

5. Create backend/app/ml/preference_dataset.py. Implement get_outfit_embeddings(outfit, vector_store) -> list[np.ndarray]: calls vector_store.fetch_embeddings([str(iid) for iid in outfit.item_ids]); returns list of np.array(v) for each iid where str(iid) is in the returned dict; wraps in try/except returning [] on error or if vector_store is None. Implement build_preference_pairs(db: Session, user_id: str, vector_store) -> list[tuple[list, list]]: imports RecommendationFeedback from app.models.recommendation_feedback and Outfit from app.models.outfit; queries db.query(RecommendationFeedback).filter(RecommendationFeedback.owner_id == uuid.UUID(user_id)).all(); joins each row with its outfit via row.outfit; separates liked (rating in ('like','worn')) and disliked (rating=='dislike'); creates cross-product pairs (liked_i, disliked_j); calls get_outfit_embeddings for each; skips pairs where either returns []; returns list of (preferred_embs, rejected_embs); entire function wrapped in try/except returning [].

6. Create backend/tests/test_preference_dataset.py. Use entirely in-memory fakes — no real DB or Pinecone. Define a FakeOutfit with .item_ids=[uuid4()]. Define a FakeVectorStore with .fetch_embeddings returning {str(iid): [0.1]*512 for iid in ids}. Define a FakeDB whose .query(...).filter(...).all() returns a list of fake RecommendationFeedback rows with .outfit and .rating attributes. Tests: (a) get_outfit_embeddings returns one 512-d array per item found. (b) get_outfit_embeddings returns [] when vector_store.fetch_embeddings returns {}. (c) build_preference_pairs with 1 liked + 1 disliked returns 1 pair. (d) build_preference_pairs skips pair when embeddings are empty. (e) build_preference_pairs returns [] when db.query raises an exception.
acceptance_criteria: backend/tests/test_outfit_compatibility_transformer.py passes: all tests green, no torch import errors
backend/tests/test_preference_dataset.py passes: all tests green (no real DB or Pinecone required)
All 16 existing tests in tests/test_recommendation_agent.py still pass (no regressions from new imports)
verification: cd backend && .\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\test_outfit_compatibility_transformer.py tests\test_preference_reward_model.py tests\test_preference_dataset.py tests\test_recommendation_agent.py -x -q
findings: All 32 tests pass (16 new + 16 existing recommendation_agent tests). Breakdown: test_outfit_compatibility_transformer.py: 5 tests; test_preference_reward_model.py: 5 tests; test_preference_dataset.py: 5 tests; test_recommendation_agent.py: 16 tests. Implementation decisions: (1) OutfitCompatibilityTransformer uses batch_first=True TransformerEncoderLayer for clean (batch, seq, d_model) tensor layout. (2) train_on_polyvore_style_data returns the trained model for testability. (3) preference_reward_model exposes module-level functions (load_or_init, save, train_from_feedback, predict_reward) that take the model as an argument, keeping the model class clean and testable. (4) _mean_pool_embeddings is exported from preference_reward_model to allow direct use in test (d). (5) preference_dataset.py uses a lazy import of RecommendationFeedback inside build_preference_pairs to avoid circular imports at module load time. (6) All torch operations wrapped in try/except; score_outfit returns 0.5 and predict_reward returns 0.0 if torch unavailable. Run time: 21.80s on CPU.
